scores.why: Scoped to manual and electric wheelchairs and prams, with adjustable step height, door width, toilet, changing table and cobble avoidance, and no disability disclosure. Covers places, walking routes and transit stops; missing data shows as incomplete, never as accessible; the map has a list alternative. The WCAG audit in the README is not reproducible from the repo.

The live web app works: place cards, scored step-free routes, a source-outage banner, moderation, an embeddable widget and an Expo mobile app. About 9.5k source lines, but only one test file (15 tests), no accessibility or end-to-end tests in CI, and user reports stored in temporary storage.

Every fact has a source, date and record link; data older than 2 years is flagged, agreement between 2+ sources marks it confirmed, conflicts are shown side by side, reports are marked unverified. A real conflict (city 2023 'yes' vs OSM 2026 'no') is visible live; imports keep the last dated copy on failure.

Ingestion adapters are separate from the shared fact model and presentation; a daily automated refresh isolates each source; Warsaw was added from config alone; public API and widget. Storage is JSON in git and hosting outside the city is described, not built.

A priced model: free for residents, Pro 29–49 zł/month for venues, 199 zł per event, usage-based API, city licence, plus a monthly cost table. No revenue scenarios or market sizing, and no Polish deck or video in the repo (only a video script).
